summary_profile.description: Diarrhoeal disease is characterized by the passage of three or more loose or liquid stools per day. It is one of the most common health problems worldwide and a major cause of malnutrition and death, especially in children under 5 years. Most cases are caused by infectious agents (viruses, bacteria, or parasites) transmitted through contaminated food or water. While most episodes are self-limiting, severe or prolonged diarrhea can lead to dangerous dehydration and electrolyte imbalance.
common_symptoms: Frequent loose or watery stools (3 or more times per day)
Low-grade fever (especially in bacterial or viral cases)
severe_symptoms: Signs of severe dehydration (sunken eyes, dry mouth, no tears, reduced urine)
causes: Viruses (Rotavirus, Norovirus, Adenovirus — most common in children)
Bacteria (Escherichia coli, Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, Vibrio cholerae)
risk_factors: Travel to areas with poor sanitation
Consumption of unsafe water or street food
diagnosis_methods: Clinical assessment based on history and symptoms
Rapid antigen tests for Rotavirus and Norovirus
Electrolyte and kidney function blood tests
treatment_options: Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) is the cornerstone of treatment
Antibiotics only for specific bacterial causes (e.g., cholera, severe shigellosis)
Antiparasitic drugs when parasites are identified
Intravenous fluids in severe dehydration or shock
medications: Zinc sulfate (20 mg/day for 10–14 days in children)
Antibiotics: Azithromycin, Ciprofloxacin, or Doxycycline (only when indicated)
Metronidazole or Tinidazole (for amoebiasis or giardiasis)
lifestyle_home_remedies: Drink plenty of clean fluids (ORS, coconut water, clear soups)
Use clean and safe drinking water
Gradually resume normal diet after improvement
diet_recommended: Khichdi, dalia, boiled rice with curd
diet_to_avoid: Dairy products (except curd/yogurt) during acute phase
complications: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (in some E. coli cases)
Persistent diarrhea leading to stunted growth in children
summary_profile.when_to_see_doctor: Seek medical care if diarrhea lasts more than 2 days, if there is blood in stool, high fever, severe dehydration, or if the patient is a young child, elderly, or has underlying health conditions.
emergency_signs: Signs of severe dehydration (very dry mouth, sunken eyes, lethargy, cold extremities)
